main_text.p: [?]mipelagianum faltèm eft; fi non Pelagianum, & ut aduerfum Dei verbo, intolerabile: fi quis, toties admonitus, & erroris convictus, pergat mordicus id defendere; publicè præsertim. Quid enim aliud vult Paulus, quando ad Tit. 3. v. 10. inquit: Hæreticum hominem, post unam & alteram admonitionem, devita: sciens, quòd subversus est talis, & peccat αὐτο-κατάκριτος[?]. v. 11. Alia est eorum ratio, de quibus Phil. 3. v. 14. Si quid aliter sapitis, & hoc Deus vobis revelabit. Verumtamen in eo, ad quod pervenimus, eádem incedamus regulâ; idem sapiamus. v. 16.

Etsi ergo veteres, ante Augustinum, omnes ita senserint, aut locuti essent; ut demonstrare hic suscipit, assumto uno atque altero ex utraque Ecclesiâ, Græcâ & Latinâ: (absque tamen causâ. Fatetur enim de seipse Augustinus, lib. 1. de Prædest. Sanct. c. 3. & lib. 1. Retract. c. 23. & Prosper de illis, Epistolâ ad Augustum. Verba Augustini sunt: Fidem elegit Deus in præscientiâ: ut, quem sibi credituræ esse præscivit, ipsum elegerit &c. Non-

page.notes: Printer's marks in the right margin beside each line (small double ornaments) are not text and are left out. The first letter of "mipelagianum" is clipped at the start of the page; it is probably "Semi-", but I have not filled it in. The Greek word after "peccat" is only partly legible; my reading αὐτο-κατάκριτος is a guess and is marked [?]. The word "dum" at the foot is the catchword for the next page, so it is not in the text. The page carries no running head and no signature.
